Routing evidence:
- Option C (“regional office”) was accepted for SOUTH-region claims (small and large) and a large SOUTH shipment.
- Option C was rejected for all EAST-region requests observed (invoice small; refund small/large).
- Option C was also rejected for a large SOUTH refund.
- Therefore, do not route EAST requests to C. For SOUTH, C appears valid for claims and at least some shipments, but not refunds.
- No evidence yet distinguishes when to use A (standard queue) versus B (priority desk), or whether size/message/sender affects routing. Avoid inferring from urgency language alone.

Routing evidence:
- Option C (“regional office”) is valid for some SOUTH requests: accepted for small/large claims and a large shipment. It was rejected for a large SOUTH refund.
- Option C was rejected for all observed EAST requests (invoice, refund, shipment, claim), and should not be used for EAST.
- Option A (“standard queue”) was accepted for an EAST small refund and a NORTH small invoice.
- Option A was rejected for: SOUTH small refund; NORTH small/large refunds and small claim; EAST small shipment and large claim.
- Therefore, A is not a general fallback. Current evidence suggests it may depend on region and request type/size, but the rule is not yet established.
- No successful B (“priority desk”) assignment has been observed. B is the remaining candidate when A and C are contradicted, but do not assume this without confirmation.
- Examples where C is contradicted and A failed: SOUTH small refund; NORTH small refund, large refund, small claim; EAST small shipment, large claim.
- Do not infer routing from urgency, sender, wording, or message details alone; similar urgency/no-urgency wording has appeared across outcomes.
- Continue tracking request type, region, size, and option result.

Routing evidence:
- C (“regional office”) is valid for SOUTH small/large shipments and small/large claims; also previously accepted for a SOUTH large shipment. It was rejected for a SOUTH large invoice and large refund. Do not assume C for all SOUTH requests.
- C has been rejected for every observed EAST request (invoice, refund, shipment, claim). Avoid C for EAST.
- A (“standard queue”) was accepted for EAST small refund and NORTH small invoice.
- A was rejected for SOUTH small refund; NORTH small/large refunds and small claim; EAST small shipment and large claim. A is not a general fallback.
- B (“priority desk”) is now confirmed valid for EAST small shipment and NORTH large shipment. It was rejected for NORTH small refund, NORTH large claim, and SOUTH small shipment. B is not a universal fallback.
- When both A and C were contradicted, outcomes include B accepted (EAST small shipment; NORTH large shipment), but B also failed in some such cases. Infer only from accumulated region/type/size evidence.
- Notable repeated result: NORTH large shipment accepted with B; SOUTH small shipment accepted with C but rejected with B.
- Do not infer routing from urgency, sender, wording, or message details; similar wording appears across outcomes.
- Continue tracking region, request type, size, and each option’s result.

Routing evidence:
- C (“regional office”) is valid for SOUTH small/large shipments and large claims; also valid for SOUTH small/large claims in prior evidence. It is rejected for SOUTH small/large refunds and large invoices. Do not assume C for all SOUTH requests.
- C has been rejected for every observed EAST request (invoice, refund, shipment, claim). Avoid C for EAST.
- A (“standard queue”) was accepted for EAST small refund and NORTH small invoice. It is not a general fallback: rejected for SOUTH small refund; NORTH small/large refunds and small claim; EAST small shipment and large claim.
- B (“priority desk”) is valid for EAST small and large shipments, NORTH small and large shipments. It was rejected for EAST small claim, NORTH small refund and large claim, and SOUTH small shipment. B is not universal.
- D has now been observed: accepted for SOUTH large invoice; rejected for NORTH large claim. Treat D as request-specific, with limited evidence.
- Repeated confirmations: NORTH large shipment → B; SOUTH small shipment → C; SOUTH large claim → C.
- When A and C are contradicted, B sometimes works (EAST shipments, NORTH shipments) but can fail (EAST small claim, NORTH large claim). Infer from accumulated region/type/size evidence only.
- Do not infer routing from urgency, sender, wording, or message details; similar wording appears across outcomes.
- Continue tracking region, request type, size, option, and result.

Routing evidence:
- C (“regional office”) is valid for SOUTH small/large shipments and large claims; also valid for SOUTH small/large claims in prior evidence. It is rejected for SOUTH small/large refunds and large invoices. Do not assume C for all SOUTH requests.
- C has been rejected for every observed EAST request. Avoid C for EAST.
- A (“standard queue”) accepted for EAST small refund, NORTH small invoice, and NORTH large invoice. Rejected for SOUTH small refund; NORTH small/large refunds and small claim; EAST small shipment, large invoice, and large claim. Not a general fallback.
- B (“priority desk”) valid for EAST small/large shipments and NORTH small/large shipments. Rejected for EAST small claim, NORTH small refund and large refund, and NORTH large claim; SOUTH small shipment. Not universal.
- D is request-specific and limited: accepted for SOUTH large invoice; rejected for NORTH large claim, EAST small claim, and NORTH small refund.
- NORTH small claim → C is now confirmed. NORTH large invoice → A is confirmed. SOUTH large shipment → C and SOUTH large claim → C remain confirmed.
- EAST small claim has now rejected D as well as previously rejected options; no valid routing option is established. EAST large invoice rejected A; C is also invalid, so do not guess.
- NORTH large refund has rejected A and B; avoid assuming C or D without evidence.
- When A and C are contradicted, B sometimes works (EAST/NORTH shipments) but can fail. Infer only from accumulated region/type/size evidence.
- Ignore urgency, sender, wording, and message details. Track region, request type, size, option, and result.

Routing evidence:
- Track only region, request type, size, option, and result; ignore urgency, sender, wording, and message details.
- C is valid for SOUTH small/large shipments and large claims; NORTH small/large claims; and NORTH small refunds. C is rejected for SOUTH small/large refunds and large invoices, and all observed EAST requests. Do not generalize beyond these cases.
- A is valid for EAST small refund, NORTH small/large invoices, and SOUTH small invoice. It is rejected for SOUTH small/large refunds, NORTH small/large refunds, NORTH small claim, EAST small shipment, large invoice, and large claim. Not a fallback.
- B is valid for EAST small/large shipments and large invoices, and NORTH small/large shipments. It is rejected for EAST small claim, SOUTH small shipment, and NORTH large claim. Avoid assuming it elsewhere.
- D is not reliable: its earlier acceptance for SOUTH large invoice is contradicted by the latest rejection. It is rejected for SOUTH large invoice, NORTH large claim, EAST small claim, and NORTH small refund.
- Confirmed recent outcomes: NORTH large claim → C; NORTH small claim → C; NORTH small refund → C; EAST large invoice → B; EAST large shipment → B; SOUTH small invoice → A.
- EAST small claim has rejected A and D; no valid option is established. SOUTH large refund rejected A, while C is already invalid; do not guess. NORTH large refund rejected A and B; avoid C/D without evidence.
- When options conflict, rely on exact accumulated region/type/size evidence; do not infer from urgency or wording.

Routing notes:
- Use only region, request type, size, option, and result. Ignore urgency, sender, wording, and message details.
- Confirmed valid assignments:
  - A: EAST small refund; NORTH small/large invoices; SOUTH small invoice.
  - B: EAST small/large shipments and large invoices.
  - C: SOUTH small shipment; SOUTH small/large claims; NORTH small claim, small refund, and large refund.
  - D: EAST small claim.
- Confirmed rejected assignments:
  - A: SOUTH small/large refunds; NORTH small/large refunds; NORTH small claim; EAST small shipment, large invoice, and large claim.
  - B: NORTH small/large shipments; NORTH large claim; EAST small claim; SOUTH small shipment.
  - C: SOUTH small/large refunds; SOUTH small claim; NORTH large claim; EAST requests observed previously, except the newly confirmed NORTH/SOUTH cases above.
  - D: SOUTH large invoice; NORTH large claim; NORTH small refund.
- The latest outcomes correct earlier assumptions: A is valid for NORTH large invoice; C for NORTH large refund and SOUTH small shipment; D for EAST small claim. B is not valid for NORTH small or large shipment. C is not valid for SOUTH small claim.
- Unresolved cases: SOUTH large refund (A and C rejected); NORTH large refund is now resolved as C; avoid guessing on any unobserved combination.
- When evidence conflicts, use the latest exact region/type/size result. Do not generalize across regions, sizes, or request types, and never infer from wording or urgency.

Routing notes:
- Use only region, request type, size, option, and result. Ignore urgency, sender, wording, and message details.
- Confirmed valid assignments:
  - A: EAST small/large refunds; NORTH small/large invoices; SOUTH small/large invoices.
  - B: EAST large shipment and large invoice. (EAST small shipment is rejected.)
  - C: SOUTH small shipment; NORTH small/large refunds.
  - D: EAST small claim and large claim.
- Confirmed rejected assignments:
  - A: SOUTH small/large refunds; NORTH small/large refunds; NORTH small claim; EAST small shipment, large invoice, and large claim.
  - B: NORTH small/large shipments; NORTH large claim; EAST small shipment and small claim; SOUTH small shipment.
  - C: SOUTH small/large refunds and claims; NORTH small claim and large claim; EAST requests observed previously, except confirmed cases above.
  - D: SOUTH large invoice; NORTH large claim and small refund.
- Recent evidence supersedes earlier assumptions: A is valid for EAST large refund and SOUTH large invoice; C is valid for NORTH large refund and SOUTH small shipment; D is valid for EAST large claim. C is rejected for NORTH small claim and SOUTH large claim. B is rejected for EAST small shipment.
- Do not generalize across regions, sizes, or request types. When evidence conflicts, use the latest exact result. Never infer from wording or urgency.
- Avoid guessing on unobserved combinations.
